sampling_model.design: The canonical experiment is one observation \(Z_h\sim N(h,\Sigma)\). Transfer from \(P_{n,h}\) is conditional on the nonstandard uniform two-sided experiment-equivalence premise, not on ordinary pointwise local asymptotic normality.
sampling_model.units: The target population is summarized locally by the reduced-form mean \(h\in H\) and the partially identified causal welfare contrast \(U^{\ast}\).
sampling_model.treatment: The rule \(\delta(Z_h)\in[0,1]\) is the fraction or probability assigned to treatment; both deterministic and randomized measurable rules are allowed.
sampling_model.overlap: No propensity-score overlap condition is imposed in the Gaussian endpoint game; feasibility is the nonempty interval \([\ell(h),u(h)]\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For transfer, \(\widehat Z_n\) is generated by the forward kernel \(K_n\) from the nonstandard two-sided experiment-equivalence premise. A sufficient construction on the standard Borel space \(\mathcal X_n\) uses a measurable statistic \(T_n\) with a uniform Gaussian-pivot error \(a_n\to0\) and an \(h\)-independent reconstruction kernel \(\mathsf R_n\) with uniform reconstruction error \(b_n\to0\); setting \(K_n(x,\cdot)=\delta_{T_n(x)}\) and \(L_n=\mathsf R_n\) gives \(\lambda_n\le a_n+b_n\). A training split constructs \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\), including \(\widehat\Sigma_n\), and is required separately to return a member of \(\mathcal G_p\) satisfying \(\mathsf B_{\kappa}\), \(P_{n,h}\)-almost surely for every \(n\) and \(h\in H\); the numerical bounds alone do not imply legal membership. A conditionally independent evaluation split constructs \(\widehat Z_n\), and uniform convergence to zero of the expected conditional total-variation distance from \(N(h,\widehat\Sigma_n)\) implies \(\gamma_n\to0\). The reference \(Q_{n,h}\) has exactly the same \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\)-marginal as \(P_{n,h}\), so legality and the numerical bounds hold under both joint laws before the certified selector is run. Primitive error is then measured by \(\alpha_n\), and the decision is computed at a strictly positive certified gap \(\varepsilon_n>0\), with \(\varepsilon_n\to0\) only along the sequence. No rate for \(a_n\), \(b_n\), or \(\lambda_n\) is asserted.

body.tldr: The new angle asks when asymmetric nonsmooth partial identification makes every minimax treatment rule genuinely multivariate. The proposal preserves the unrestricted measurable-rule saddle theorem, face-complete least-favorable priors, convergent global exchange bounds, and the asymmetric triangular coexistence witness, but moves the theorem-level frontier to a finite curved-score certificate. In two dimensions, exact primal-dual closure for a finite endpoint prior, noncancellation of its analytic Gaussian-mixture score, and one regular zero-set arc with curvature bounded away from zero imply a unique minimax rule and exclude every measurable one-index representation. The answer-open task is to construct an unbalanced rational endpoint prior and outward-rounded interval certificate satisfying these conditions, or prove that no such two-dimensional game exists. The full all-one-index, coexistence, or no-one-index normal-fan classification remains open. Every finite exchange tolerance is strictly positive; limiting tolerances may converge to zero. Feasible transfer is retained only as a conditional secondary corollary under two-sided experiment equivalence, legal bounded game estimation, and joint total-variation approximation, with no named-model or rate claim.

project_justification.gap: Theorem 3 of MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local is the feasible fully differentiable result. Its Assumption 5(i) imposes convexity and centrosymmetry for directionally differentiable bounds, Theorem 4 supplies selected rules for that limit game, Theorem 5 gives their feasible transfer, and the Conclusion leaves the joint directional-differentiability and non-centrosymmetry regime open. Yata2025Optimal relies on an antipodal modulus pair. MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision imposes open-set sign ambiguity and establishes multiplicity without classifying the full unrestricted correspondence; the present primitive class instead uses a weaker pointwise sign-ambiguity condition. AradillasFernandezMontielOleaQiuStoyeTinda2026RobustBayes solves ex-ante \(\Gamma\)-MMR and ex-post \(\Gamma\)-PER under its equation-(2.9) constrained prior class and derives uniqueness, randomization, and linear-index threshold conclusions, but does not solve the unrestricted endpoint-state minimax-regret correspondence or exclude arbitrary measurable one-index rules. The corrected-proof Abstract of ChristensenMoonSchorfheide2026OptimalDecisionRules derives asymptotically optimal discrete-choice rules from a hybrid objective: minimax ambiguity treatment for the partially identified payoff parameter conditional on a point-identified parameter, combined with average-risk minimization for the point-identified parameter. That objective is orthogonal to the exact unrestricted signed-endpoint minimax-regret saddle studied here, and neither objective implies the other.
project_justification.niche: Finite endpoint priors produce analytic differences of Gaussian mixtures. Their global primal-dual gap and local boundary jets are finite objects that can certify properties of the entire unrestricted minimax correspondence, including failure of every scalar-index representation.
project_justification.fill: The project derives unrestricted saddle duality and face-complete dual representatives, then proves that exact finite-prior saddle closure plus a nonvanishing curved Bayes-score boundary yields uniqueness and the no-one-index category. Convergent exchange bounds locate candidate priors, while outward-rounded interval arithmetic closes the global risk inequalities and the local curvature inequalities. The triangular value-\(2/3\) construction remains the coexistence regression test, and the complete normal-fan trichotomy remains answer-open. Conditional feasible transfer is secondary and makes no statistical frontier or rate claim.

body.related_work: Montiel Olea, Qiu, and Stoye, \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision}, establish multiplicity and qualified failure of linear threshold rules in partially identified treatment choice, but do not exclude every randomized measurable rule based on one linear projection. Montiel Olea, Qiu, and Stoye, \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local}, solve the smooth asymmetric and nonsmooth centrosymmetric regimes separately and leave their joint relaxation open; the present compact asymmetric polyhedral class occupies that orthogonal regime, not a superclass of their full Assumption-5 class. Yata, \cite{Yata2025Optimal}, obtains an optimal one-index rule from an antipodal modulus pair under centrosymmetry, providing the positive benchmark that the curved-score certificate can falsify outside symmetry. Aradillas Fernández, Montiel Olea, Qiu, Stoye, and Tinda, \cite{AradillasFernandezMontielOleaQiuStoyeTinda2026RobustBayes}, use the constrained ambiguity specification in their equation (2.9), with a symmetric uniform two-point distribution over the reduced-form parameter and unrestricted compatible conditional distributions, and Theorems 1--2 analyze ex-ante \(\Gamma\)-MMR and ex-post \(\Gamma\)-PER rules with uniqueness, randomization, and linear-index threshold conclusions. Those results are orthogonal to the present unrestricted minimax-regret saddle: Nature here ranges over every signed endpoint state, and the curved-score theorem excludes every arbitrary measurable one-index rule \(g(w^{\top}z)\), not only linear threshold rules. Christensen, Moon, and Schorfheide, \cite{ChristensenMoonSchorfheide2026OptimalDecisionRules}, derive asymptotically optimal discrete-choice rules under partial identification by combining minimax ambiguity treatment for the partially identified payoff parameter conditional on a point-identified parameter with average-risk minimization for that point-identified parameter; this description is anchored to the Abstract of the corrected proof dated 13 March 2026. Their hybrid asymptotic objective and the present exact unrestricted signed-endpoint minimax-regret objective are orthogonal, neither objective implies the other, and the present curved-score result concerns exclusion of every arbitrary measurable one-index rule rather than asymptotic efficiency for learning the point-identified parameter. Tetenov, \cite{Tetenov2012Asymmetric}, derives threshold structure for point-identified asymmetric regret, showing that asymmetry alone does not generate the proposed non-index phenomenon. Teicher, \cite{Teicher1963Mixtures}, supplies finite-normal-mixture identifiability, while Zahm et al., \cite{ZahmEtAl2020Ridge}, formalize ridge functions as measurable functions of linear projections and study gradient diagnostics; neither source links analytic mixture-score geometry to uniqueness of an unrestricted minimax treatment rule. Aradillas Fernández et al., \cite{AradillasFernandezEtAl2025Epsilon}, optimize mixtures over a fixed finite rule menu, and Zhang, Wu, and López, \cite{ZhangWuLopez2010Exchange}, treat convex semi-infinite exchange with finite-dimensional primals. The proposed exchange construction instead preserves the exact measurable-rule Bayes envelope and requests only strictly positive finite tolerances. The deeper scan located no paper giving an exact unbalanced least-favorable endpoint distribution, a curved Gaussian-mixture Bayes boundary, and a global certificate excluding every one-index minimax rule. Hirano and Porter, \cite{HiranoPorter2009}, remain pointwise limit-experiment motivation only; the secondary feasible corollary is explicitly conditional on stronger two-sided and joint total-variation premises.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The curved-score theorem is a sufficient certificate, not the requested necessary-and-sufficient normal-fan classification. Its global premise must be closed by exact inequalities; a plot or floating-point near-zero gap is insufficient. The value-\(2/3\) triangular witness establishes coexistence, not the no-one-index branch. Face completeness concerns only faces charged by some dual optimum. Exchange iterates use exact restricted-game and worst-state oracles, make no complexity-rate claim, and request a strictly positive tolerance at every finite run; no finite termination at tolerance zero is asserted. The conditional transfer corollary requires two-sided experiment equivalence, legal \(\kappa\)-bounded estimated games, and joint total-variation approximation, none of which follows from ordinary DQM or pointwise LAN.
body.honest_scope: The theorem-level frontier is exact decision geometry in a two-dimensional compact polyhedral Gaussian endpoint game. The all-saddle theorem and face-complete priors hold in general dimension, the triangular construction certifies coexistence, and the curved-score theorem gives a finite sufficient route to the no-one-index category. The existence of a rational unbalanced witness satisfying that route and the full finite primitive trichotomy are open-ended questions. As a sanity check, the centered antipodal specialization recovers Yata's selected one-index rule, while the compact-polyhedral overlap with Theorem 4 of Montiel Olea--Qiu--Stoye has the identical objective by construction; no containment of their full Assumption-5 class is asserted. Conditional feasible transfer is secondary, has no named-model instantiation or rate claim, and uses only strictly positive finite certificate tolerances tending to zero along a sequence.
